First, we went on a trip and used two tanks of gas. One tank was used when we left our home city, and the other was used on the way back. I used my company gas card to fill up the tank when we left, and that tank was empty before we started. When my friend went to fill up the tank on the way home, he asked for half the money, but I said no because I provided us with an entire tank to get to the destination. My friend's argument is that since I didn't pay for the gas myself, it doesn't count. But I think it does count because I still supplied us with half the tank, and the method of acquiring the gas shouldn't matter. Also, we used his car for the trip, but we had used my car for the last trip, which was roughly the same distance, and it was his turn to provide the vehicle. So, is it morally acceptable for me not to directly pay him for half the gas? I'm not sure. On one hand, I provided the gas for the trip, so maybe I don't owe him anything. On the other hand, he's asking for half the money, and maybe he feels like he's contributing by providing the car, so he deserves something in return. I also wonder if there's an unspoken agreement between us about how we split costs when we use each other's cars. Maybe we should have talked about this beforehand to avoid confusion. But since we didn't, how do I decide what's fair now? Another thing to consider is whether the gas I provided was a gift or if it's expected that I would be reimbursed. Since I used my company gas card, maybe it's not my personal money, but it's still a resource I have access to. Does that change anything? I also think about the fairness of using each other's cars. We alternated providing the vehicle, so maybe that's a fair way to split the costs. But if one person's car is more expensive to maintain or has higher gas consumption, does that affect how we should split the costs? Overall, I'm trying to balance the resources I provided (the gas) with the resources my friend provided (the car). I don't want to take advantage of him, but I also don't think I should have to pay for something I already covered. Maybe we need to have a conversation to clarify our expectations and find a mutually acceptable solution. In the end, I'm leaning towards it being morally acceptable not to directly pay him for half the gas because I already provided the necessary resources for the trip. However, I should communicate with him to ensure he feels fairly treated and to prevent any hard feelings.
